html:
SMTO-TSK-0047 — The task was stopped before these commands ran

GUID: 1f915c56-57ec-4376-952a-f4b4b321dadc
Slug: run-stopping
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • You asked to stop the task while SMTO was getting a group of commands ready, so it did not start them. None of the commands in this group were run at this point.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the task in the conversation shows as stopped, and that you or someone else selected Stop on it. This message only appears when a stop request reached the task before the commands were started.
  2. Read the task's earlier results in the conversation to see what was already done before you stopped it. Work from earlier steps stays done; only this group of commands was skipped.
  3. If you still want the commands run, send a new message asking for them. A new request starts the commands fresh; SMTO will not restart them on its own.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as stopped with this group of commands not run, and a new request, if you send one, runs normally.

If it still fails

  • If tasks stop like this when nobody selected Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same request over and over while the cause is unclear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • shell__sequence preflight rejected the sequence (error_kind run_stopping, executed_steps 0) because the shared inference budget check raised UserCancelled: the task's cancellation event was set.

What this means

  • A shell-sequence checkpoint catches RuntimeError from the shared budget check, whose current matching branch raises UserCancelled when the cancellation event is set; it rejects the next child before dispatch. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A shell-sequence checkpoint catches RuntimeError from the shared budget check, whose current matching branch raises UserCancelled when the cancellation event is set; it rejects the next child before dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the cancellation event and completed child prefix; a separate wall-clock policy exception is not this RuntimeError branch.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No repair is needed: the run's cancel_event was set (Stop) when the sequence preflight called InferenceBudget.check, so no child shell command was dispatched. Inspect the run's sequence events and receipts to confirm executed_steps is 0; any further work must be requested as a new task, not an automatic retry.

Retry and execution caution

  • This state requests no new execution or automatic retry. Inspect the current task controls and retained results.

How to verify the fix

  • The original sequence records its completed prefix and starts no further child after this cancellation checkpoint.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
